messages.subject: how mergeStrands works
parts:
For SNP6.0, summarization for total copy number analysis is done as
the following:

>AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=+300)

I want to know how the argument [mergeStrands=TRUE] works? What is
expected if mergeStrands is set to FALSE? I assume that the affinities
are different between the CN probe for the plus strand and the same CN
probe for the minus strand (or, sense and anti-sense),

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] how mergeStrands works
parts:
On Tue, Aug 19, 2008 at 9:37 AM, JP <playb...@yahoo.com> wrote:
>
> For SNP6.0, summarization for total copy number analysis is done as
> the following:
>
>>AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=+300)
>
> I want to know how the argument [mergeStrands=TRUE] works? What is
> expected if mergeStrands is set to FALSE? I assume that the affinities
> are different between the CN probe for the plus strand and the same CN
> probe for the minus strand (or, sense and anti-sense),

For GWS5 & GWS6 arrays, 'mergeStrands' has no effect. This is because
for those chip types, there are no SNPs for which we have data on both
strands*, only either or, so there is nothing to merge. (* on GWS5
there is indeed a few SNPs for which one allele is interrogated by
probes on one strand and the other allele by probes on the opposite
strand. However, we treat those rare cases as if they are one the
same strand). CN loci are treated independently and since there is
only one CN probe per loci, there is nothing to model. I don't think
there are CN probes from different strands at the same loci, at least
does the Affymetrix CDFs not couple CN probes this way (they have
always done it for SNPs).

The reason why I put 'mergeStrands=TRUE' in the vignettes/example code
is to avoid the mistake that someone one day take the same code and
run it on, say 500K data. Also, it might be that Affymetrix release a
new chip where they have probe pairs on both strands, so it is always
safer to do 'mergeStrands=TRUE'.

The AvgCnPlm is not a multi-array method that models probe affinities.
It only takes the median probe signal across all probes. You will
get more details on this as soon we can get the paper out.

/Henrik
